openings.claim: Provisionally retain the plate with two slot-mounted mechanical saddles that capture nonworking corners and open for inspection.
openings.delta: Change the retention carrier from variable magnetic attraction to bent steel-strip contact stops and movable hold-downs. Use two strips as slot-anchored bases with corner lips, two as pivoting hold-downs, and cork at contact surfaces. Drill only strips; use existing slots and supplied bolts. Position all hardware outside the stroke clearance and marked working edge.
openings.prediction: If the saddles restrain both in-plane directions and lift without excessive play, both plates should remain within 1 mm after twenty strokes despite their different magnetic pull checks. The nearest rival, magnet retention, could show plate-dependent slip; equal stability would leave that rival viable.
openings.probe: First use ruler and unfastened strips to check whether the slots permit two corner captures, bolt access, an exposed working edge and clearance throughout the stroke. Stop if that envelope fails. If feasible, fabricate within eighty minutes. Compare mechanical saddles with a magnet configuration only if magnets also fit the permitted envelope. Use at most three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks per configuration within twenty observation minutes. Include the spare plate and thick gloves in the final run/check. Mark reference positions away from the working edge; measure displacement and time complete return.
assumptions: Unprovided slot dimensions and locations allow strip anchoring and corner capture without forbidden modification.
Strips can be bent using pliers; bolt lengths, strip stiffness and available clearance are sufficient.

Loosening captive pivot bolts with the screwdriver permits gloved removal/return within sixty seconds without edge contact. Failure defeats serviceability; displacement above 1 mm defeats retention. Neither capacity is established.

assessment: A bounded fabrication and comparison probe, not deployment. Geometry, mechanical capacity and gloved service time remain unknown; do not fabricate if the initial fit check cannot preserve every constraint.
